verdict.rationale: mise documents running `mise install` in a cloned project directory to install the tools declared in `mise.toml`, and pitches a fresh laptop as `git clone` plus `mise bootstrap`. `mise install --locked` adds reproducibility, and community users confirm that new contributors get set up with one command, with postinstall hooks also pulling in dependencies. missing for 10: first-party documentation that `[hooks] postinstall` extends the one command to project dependencies beyond tools (only community reports cover it).

support.subject: As a developer, I can bootstrap a fresh clone with one command that installs everything the project declares

citations.quote: run `mise install` in the project directory and `mise tasks ls` to list its tasks.
declare which ones a project uses in `mise.toml`.
mise replaces them with one file that's checked in, so a fresh laptop is `git clone` and `mise bootstrap`.
For reproducible installs, commit a [lockfile](/dev-tools/mise-lock.html) and run `mise install --locked`.
I always setup a postinstall hook so someone just runs `mise install` and gets correct tool versions plus dependencies installed.
It makes it so much easier for new people to get started without having to do a bunch of manual steps.
